subject: Private deployment: Branch capacity top-up + term update
messages:
From: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@cardiota.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.k@cardiota.com>, procurement@cardiota.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + additional branch site (San Antonio) request

Hi Alex,

We're approaching our Redwood renewal in mid-July and we need to add a new private branch in our San Antonio footprint. Current setup: 2 clusters (prod/eu & prod/us) with VPC boundaries. The ask:

- Add an additional on-prem site (San Antonio) with the same isolation guarantees as our current private deployment.
- Baseline capacity for the new site: 4 inference nodes (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), ability to burst to 8 during batch windows.
- Adjust term to align with our enterprise contract renewal (new 12-month term to start on the renewal date).

Attached is a rough provisioning matrix from our infra team. Can you confirm whether this is doable at renewal and provide an estimate for committed vs burst pricing? Also flag any changes to SLA or lead times for on-prem provisioning.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround,
Elaine
VP Engineering
Cardiota Systems

Attachment: cardiota_provisioning_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@cardiota.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + additional branch site (San Antonio) request

Hi Elaine — thanks for the details and the matrix. Looping in Rishi for pricing and Tessa for provisioning / lead times. High-level: we can support an additional isolated on-prem footprint and mirror your existing isolation model, but there are two things to confirm before I hand to Rishi/Tessa:

1) Do you want the San Antonio site to be added as a new "environment" under the same private control plane, or completely separated (separate control plane / air-gapped)? (This affects lead time and costs.)
2) Are there specific compliance controls (custom KMS/HSM, additional audit retention) required that differ from your existing sites?

If you can confirm those two points, Rishi can provide committed vs burst pricing and Tessa can give a provisioning timeline.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine@cardiota.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + additional branch site (San Antonio) request

Hi Elaine — quick pricing note based on the matrix and the two sizing options Alex called out. Assumptions: 4 baseline nodes, 8 burst nodes; identical isolation profile (same VPC + private control plane).

Option A — Shared control plane (single private control plane; separate VPC/cluster):
- Committed 12-month baseline (4 nodes): $120,000 / year (flat committed spend)
- Burst capacity (on-demand add 4 nodes): $1.80 per GPU-hour
- Lead time for provisioning: 4–6 weeks (standard)

Option B — Separate control plane (fully isolated, separate control plane & KMS):
- Committed 12-month baseline (4 nodes): $165,000 / year (premium for isolated control plane)
- Burst capacity (on-demand): $2.40 per GPU-hour
- Lead time for provisioning: 8–10 weeks (requires config + security review)

Notes:
- If you need dedicated HSM integration, add $12k one-time for integration and $2k / month managed HSM ops.
- We can front-load a portion of the baseline (60%) to reduce immediate lead-time for hardware ordering; will confirm with Tessa.

Action items:
- Elaine: confirm shared vs separate control plane preference and whether HSM/KMS changes are needed.
- Tessa: will confirm lead-time windows and whether a faster procurement path (expedite) is possible and the delta in cost.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_scenarios_summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine@cardiota.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + additional branch site (San Antonio) request

Thanks — quick operational reply. If Cardiota chooses Option A (shared control plane), our provisioning path is:

- Week 0–1: Contract amendment executed; procure initial hardware allocation.
- Week 2–3: Build and test cluster (networking + KV cache configuration mirroring prod).
- Week 4–6: Secure install (onsite engineer or partner), connectivity testing, and final handoff.

If Option B (separate control plane): add a 4-week security review slot (we book this with security & infra), and do a dry-run in our staging environment before on-prem install.

Expedite: We have an expedite path (available once a purchase order + 60% of committed baseline invoice is issued). Expedite reduces typical lead times by ~2 weeks but requires supply confirmation.

I'll attach a provisioning checklist after we confirm control plane choice.

—Tessa
Senior Deployment Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@cardiota.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + additional branch site (San Antonio) request

Alex / Rishi / Tessa — thanks for the quick turn. We've reviewed Option A/Option B with internal stakeholders. Decision:

- Go with Option A (shared private control plane, separate VPC/cluster for San Antonio).
- No additional HSM/KMS requirements at this time.
- Please prepare a term amendment that extends our enterprise agreement for 12 months from our renewal date (effective 2027-07-20) and adds the 4-node committed baseline with the burst profile as quoted.

Procurement notes: please send the draft amendment + order form. We'll route through our procurement and expect a PO within 5 business days after DocuSign. Also include the expedite path pricing & the lead-time estimate so the PO can indicate if we choose to fast-track.

Best,
Elaine Cho
VP Engineering | Cardiota Systems

Attachment: redwood_term_amendment_draft.pdf (proposed amendment)
